--- original
+++ modified
@@ -0,0 +1,59 @@
+---
+assignees:
+- claude-code
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: '8280'
+title: 'Terminal output spike: prove Noora on macOS 27, or choose the ANSI fallback'
+---
+## What
+
+cli-plan.md §5.2. This is a spike, and not an adoption. It decides which
+package draws the spinner, the progress bar and the table that the
+`doctor`, `config` and progress work all need.
+
+No package in this family uses a terminal UI library today, so there is
+no precedent and no migration cost.
+
+Build a throwaway executable in the scratch directory (NOT in this
+repository's `Sources/`) that:
+
+1. Declares `github.com/tuist/Noora` and builds on macOS 27 with
+   swift-tools-version 6.2.
+2. Draws one spinner, one progress bar that a loop advances, and one
+   three-column table.
+3. Writes every one of them to **stderr**, and writes nothing when
+   stderr is not a terminal.
+
+Report the result in a comment on this task: does it build, does it fit,
+and what is its dependency tail?
+
+If Noora does not build, does not support macOS 27, or brings a large
+dependency tail, choose the fallback: about 200 lines of our own ANSI in
+`Sources/acp-agent/Terminal/`. We need a spinner, a bar, a table and
+three colors, and nothing more.
+
+- [ ] Declare Noora in a scratch package and build it on macOS 27
+- [ ] Draw a spinner, a bar and a table
+- [ ] Prove the stderr-only and not-a-terminal rules
+- [ ] Record the verdict and the dependency tail in a task comment
+- [ ] If the verdict is no, write the ANSI fallback design in the comment
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+
+- [ ] A task comment states the verdict, the Noora version tried, the
+      dependency tail, and the reason.
+- [ ] The chosen approach draws nothing at all when stderr is a pipe.
+- [ ] The chosen approach never writes to stdout.
+- [ ] No scratch code lands in this repository. The result of this task
+      is the decision, plus the comment.
+
+## Tests
+
+- [ ] `Tests/FoundationModelsACPAgentTests/TerminalOutputTests.swift`:
+      one test that pins the decision — the renderer chosen by this
+      spike writes nothing when its destination is not a terminal. It
+      uses a `Pipe`, and it asserts the captured bytes are empty.
+- [ ] `swift test --filter TerminalOutputTests` passes.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write failing tests first, then implement to make them pass.
\ No newline at end of file
